data.title: Bob's Watches Founder Paul Altieri Unveils Private Collection of Vintage Rolex Watches in New Book, "NOT FOR SALE"
data.description:
NEWPORT BEACH, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Paul Altieri, founder and CEO of Bob's Watches, the leading online marketplace for pre-owned and vintage Rolex watches, reveals his private collection in NOT FOR SALE: A Private Collection of Vintage Rolex Watches, a 368-page hardcover coffee table book featuring 134 timepieces and the stories of the people who owned them.

For a man whose business is buying and selling watches, these are the pieces he chose to keep. The collection wasn't assembled to represent every reference or year. Instead, it reflects Altieri's personal interests, relationships, and decades of experience with vintage Rolex.

"Almost every watch in these pages came to me directly from its original owner or their family," Altieri writes in the introduction. "That is the detail I am proudest of, because it means the watches arrived with their stories still attached."

Notable Vintage Rolex Watches Featured in the Book

  • Rolex Dato-Compax (Ref. 6236): A stainless-steel triple-calendar chronograph discovered by a 14-year-old in the rough beside the 14th fairway at Pebble Beach. After going unclaimed at the clubhouse, he traded it to his brother for a skateboard, later bought it back with an eight-track player, and wore it for decades before learning its horological significance in Altieri's showroom.
  • Rolex "Paul Newman Panda" Daytona (Ref. 6263): A circa-1972 chronograph gifted by a wife to celebrate her husband earning his pilot's license. Throughout his service in the Canadian military, he routinely left the watch beneath a towel on a hook during morning swims-only for his wife to surprise him decades later by producing the original purchase papers when they sold it to Altieri.
  • Rolex Submariner "Big Crown" (Ref. 6538): A four-line dive watch-a reference famously worn by James Bond-featuring a tropical dial that has naturally aged from black to a warm caramel brown.
  • Rolex "John Player Special" Daytona (Ref. 6241): Altieri chose this black-and-gold Daytona for the cover because of its personal significance to him. "I had the good fortune of knowing Paul Newman and was always impressed by which watch he wore," actor Dylan McDermott says in the book. "This John Player Special is pure art!"

Not every meaningful watch in the book is among the rarest. Altieri bought the Rolex Submariner Ref. 16610 to mark the birth of his second child, and it's still the watch he wears every day. Of the 134 watches in the book, Brian Williams, the father-in-law of Altieri's daughter, chose that Submariner as his favorite - for both its patina and its significance. "This is Paul's day-to-day watch," Williams writes. "It's been around. It's comfortable, it's comforting . . . and it's perfect."

"This is not a buying guide, and it is not a study of market values," Altieri writes. "It is a personal look at a collection built over many years on passion and trust."

The Rolex book is available through Bob's Watches at https://www.bobswatches.com/rolex-book-not-for-sale.html. More than a decade in development, the hardcover was printed in Italy by Faenza Group, and it comes in a clamshell presentation case.

Author: Bob's Watches
Publisher: Gilt Press, LLC
Length: 368 pages
Featured collection: 134 vintage Rolex watches

Bob's Watches is a leading online marketplace for Rolex watches, providing a transparent platform to buy, sell, and trade luxury timepieces. Led by founder and CEO Paul Altieri, Bob's Watches combines authenticated watch expertise with in-depth editorial coverage of horological history, collecting, and craftsmanship. data.title: U.S. News Announces the 2027 Best Vehicle Brand and Best CPO Program Awards
data.description:
U.S. News Announces the 2027 Best Vehicle Brand and Best CPO Program Awards

U.S. News Announces the 2027 Best Vehicle Brand and Best CPO Program Awards

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Nov. 19, 2026

Mazda wins Best Car Brand, while Lexus celebrates its 10th consecutive Best Certified Pre-Owned Program award.

Summary

  • Hyundai captures two awards, earning the Best Electric Vehicle Brand while securing its third consecutive win for Best SUV Brand.
  • Mazda claims the Best Car Brand title.
  • Lexus marks a decade of excellence, earning its 10th consecutive Best Certified Pre-Owned Program title for its comprehensive warranty coverage and premium ownership perks.

WASHINGTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- U.S. News & World Report, the global authority in rankings and consumer advice, today announced its 2027 Best Vehicle Brand and Best Certified Pre-Owned Program awards.

U.S. News' Best Vehicle Brands awards evaluate 39 automakers to identify industry-wide excellence across six key segments of the automotive market. These awards recognize brands that excel in critical areas, including performance, safety and the overall quality of the interior design and technology across standard, luxury and electric vehicle (EV) segments.

Separately, the U.S. News Best CPO Program award evaluates automotive certified pre-owned vehicle programs across the industry to identify the brand that offers consumers the most benefits and peace of mind.

2027 winners:

  • Best Car Brand: Mazda
  • Best SUV Brand: Hyundai
  • Best Truck Brand: Ram 
  • Best Luxury Brand: Genesis
  • Best Electric Vehicle Brand: Hyundai
  • Best Luxury Electric Vehicle Brand: Lucid
  • Best Certified Pre-Owned Program: Lexus 

The 2027 Best Vehicle Brand Awards

Mazda captured the title of Best Car Brand for the first time since 2021, driven by the timeless styling, engaging driving dynamics, overall refinement and upscale cabins of the Mazda3 and MX-5 Miata. Hyundai earned its debut win as the Best Electric Vehicle Brand on the strength of its versatile, consumer-friendly EV duo, the Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 9. Additionally, the exceptional quality of the Palisade, Tucson and Santa Fe models helped Hyundai claim its third consecutive title for the Best SUV Brand. In the luxury electric category, Lucid takes home its second trophy as the Best Luxury Electric Vehicle Brand, while Genesis also repeated as Best Luxury Brand, thanks to standout marks across its premium lineup. In the truck segment, Ram extended its Best Truck Brand winning streak to eight years behind the strength of its Ram 1500 and Ram 2500 models.  

"With prices and financing costs top of mind for today's buyers, navigating the modern car market can feel overwhelming," said Alex Kwanten, U.S. News Autos' managing editor. "Our Best Vehicle Brand awards cut through the noise to spotlight the automakers delivering consistently great quality, reliability and everyday value across their lineups."

To determine the award winners, U.S. News averaged the overall score of all the given brand's products in each award class. The vehicle scores are derived from the U.S. News Best Cars rankings, which take into account a range of data points like safety ratings and reliability, as well as the consensus opinion of the automotive press and our own vehicle testing experts. The brand with the highest average score was designated the winner in that specific category.

The 2027 Best Certified Pre-Owned Program Award Winner

Lexus' L/Certified CPO program remains the benchmark for certified pre-owned warranty coverage, securing its 10th consecutive Best Certified Pre-Owned Program award thanks to its industry-leading coverage and luxury perks like complimentary maintenance and service loaners.

"Lexus continues to set the gold standard by backing its vehicles with an unmatched combination of long-term warranty protection, dependable road assistance and ownership perks that offer used-car buyers a stress-free experience and eliminate financial surprises down the road," says Kwanten.

To determine the award winner, U.S. News evaluated a range of distinct CPO program coverages and benefits, including warranty coverage duration, trip interruption reimbursement, roadside assistance perks, and inspection standards.

For more information, visit Best Vehicle Brands and Best Certified Pre-Owned Programs and use #BestVehicleBrands and #BestCPO on Instagram, X, LinkedIn,  TikTok and Facebook.

About U.S. News Best Cars
Since 2007, U.S. News Best Cars, the automotive channel of U.S. News & World Report, has published rankings and reviews of the majority of new vehicles sold in America. Each year, U.S. News also publishes the Best Cars Awards, including Best Vehicle Brands, Best Cars for the Money, Best Cars for Families and Best Adventure Vehicles. U.S. News Best Cars supports car shoppers throughout the entire car buying journey, offering industry-leading advice for researching cars and finding cars for sale, as well as its U.S. News Best Price Program.

About U.S. News & World Report
U.S. News & World Report is the global leader for journalism that empowers consumers, citizens, business leaders and policy officials to make confident decisions in all aspects of their lives and communities. A multifaceted media company, U.S. News provides unbiased rankings, independent reporting and analysis, and consumer advice to millions of people on USNews.com each month. A pillar in Washington for more than 90 years, U.S. News is the trusted home for in-depth and exclusive insights on education, health, politics, the economy, insurance, personal finance, travel, automobiles, real estate, careers and consumer products and services.

data.title: Flexxible Launches FlexxSolve, an AI That Fixes Employees’ IT and Tech Problems on Its Own
data.description:
Flexxible Launches FlexxSolve, an AI That Fixes Employees’ IT and Tech Problems on Its Own

Now available in the U.S. and Canada, FlexxSolve has no per-device fees and no platform to buy. Companies pay based on results.

Flexxible today launches FlexxSolve in the U.S. and Canada. FlexxSolve is an Autonomous IT tool for the workspace that uses AI to fix everyday tech problems, so employees don’t have to wait for the IT help desk. When something goes wrong with a laptop or an app, FlexxSolve finds the cause, fixes it and checks that the fix worked — always within the rules each company sets.

Flexxible’s software already runs on more than one million work devices around the world. The company has an established team in the United States, which will support FlexxSolve customers across the U.S. and Canada. Flexxible was founded in Barcelona, Spain, 18 years ago.

In its first customer deployments, FlexxSolve has fixed about 20% of IT support requests from day one. As its knowledge base about the company grows, that rises to an average of about 50%. On average, FlexxSolve fixes a problem in just seven minutes, any time of day or night.

FlexxSolve is also simple to buy and quick to start. Companies don’t need to buy a bigger platform first or set up complex integrations, and there’s no per-device fee. Instead, pricing is based on outcomes: companies pay one price when FlexxSolve fully fixes a problem, and another when it diagnoses the issue and passes it to an IT engineer. They also set their own spending limit. There’s no setup required, so problems can be fixed right away.

“Every organization, from the largest enterprise to a business of one, will end up running Autonomous IT, whether it sets out to or not,” said Sebastian Prat, founder and CEO of Flexxible. “Getting there should not take buying a platform, and companies should pay for problems solved, not for devices counted. People will stop waiting for IT support, and before long most of them will stop needing to ask for it. What makes that safe is control. The customer writes the rules and can read back everything the AI has done.”

Employees chat with FlexxSolve the way they would message a co-worker, and it can help with more than just IT. They can ask it everyday questions about the company, such as “What are the hex codes for our brand colors?” “How do I correct a purchase order we sent to a supplier?” and “How many vacation days do I have left?” They can also ask it to act for them: say “Request the day after Thanksgiving off,” and FlexxSolve files the request in the HR system. The IT team decides which company systems FlexxSolve can securely connect to, and every action it takes is recorded. Some customers already see it as a productivity tool as much as a support channel.

How FlexxSolve works:

  • It builds a hybrid knowledge base for each company. Flexxible’s AI and the company’s IT team write and edit it together. The more it covers, the more FlexxSolve can fix. The AI model itself is not trained on customer data.
  • Companies decide how much it does on its own. For each type of problem, FlexxSolve can walk a technician through the fix, wait for a person to approve it, or handle it by itself.
  • Everything is governed and private. FlexxSolve only acts within the rules and procedures the company sets, so its behavior is predictable, and every action is logged so it can be audited.

FlexxSolve also works with Microsoft Intune, the device management tool many companies already use. When Intune flags a device as out of compliance, FlexxSolve finds out exactly why — for example, because BitLocker encryption has been turned off — so it can be fixed. It also spots when Intune’s records are wrong, such as a device that looks offline but is still running, or an app that Intune says isn’t installed but is actually working. As a workspace AI tool, FlexxSolve can also work as part of FlexxClient, Flexxible’s digital employee experience (DEX) platform, to increase autonomous resolution rates. Companies that use both get one platform that manages and tracks the health and history of every device and fixes problems as they come up.

“FlexxSolve is the most important product we have built in 18 years as a company,” Prat said.

FlexxSolve is available now in the U.S. and Canada. Companies can try it free on their first 100 IT issues at flexxible.com/en/flexxsolve.

About Flexxible

Flexxible makes software that manages work devices and improves the tech experience of the people who use them. Founded in Barcelona in 2008, the company has operations in the United States, the United Kingdom, Spain, Brazil and India, and its technology runs on more than one million devices worldwide. Flexxible is recognized in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Digital Employee Experience (DEX) Management Tools. It holds ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications for information security, cloud security and privacy, and is certified at the High level of Spain’s National Security Framework (ENS).

Performance figures are averages observed in customer deployments to date. They are not a guarantee of results, which depend on each organization’s environment.

data.title: Trump Announces $17 Billion in Southeast Asia Deals
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong and Amanda Lee

The U.S. has secured a series of investment and trade deals across Southeast Asia as it seeks to expand its economic presence in the region.

President Trump announced more than $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments benefiting U.S. companies following a two-day state visit to the Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit, the White House said Wednesday.

Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced deals aimed at narrowing the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines by increasing Philippine imports of American energy and agricultural products, the White House said.

Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion deal to supply Philippine Airlines with up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft. Washington also plans to pursue a military financing package worth more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with U.S. defense equipment.

The U.S. and Thailand also made substantial progress toward a trade agreement that would eliminate tariffs on 99% of goods once signed and remove barriers to U.S. exports of vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals and agricultural products.

Thailand also plans to spend up to $123 million on U.S.-made High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems, the White House said.

In Indonesia, U.S.-based Latitude Energy and sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced talks on a $2 billion project to use American technology to improve the country's use of its coal resources.

U.S.-based Navajo Transitional Energy also signed a three-year, $100 million agreement to supply coal from its mine in southern Montana to Malaysia's TNB Fuel Services, a fuel procurement unit of utility Tenaga Nasional.

The announcements come as Southeast Asian economies grapple with higher U.S. tariffs while negotiating trade agreements with Washington.

Trade in goods and services between the U.S. and Asean totaled an estimated $686 billion in 2025, up 20.3% from 2024, according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.

data.title: Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Lenovo Group reported robust sales in the fiscal second quarter, on track to achieve its $100 billion annual revenue goal thanks to strong artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand.

Surging demand for AI servers and enterprise infrastructure has enabled the world's largest personal-computer maker to achieve better-than-expected results recently, offsetting a broader downturn in global PC shipments.

The company on Thursday said revenue for the three months ended September jumped 48% from a year earlier to $30.24 billion, beating market expectations.

Its adjusted net profit more than doubled to $1.36 billion, higher than analysts' estimate of $1.27 billion in a Visible Alpha poll. However, its bottom line was hit by a noncash fair-value loss arising from the revaluation of warrants, resulting in net loss of $640 million.

The company's infrastructure-solutions business, encompassing data-center hardware like AI servers, remained the biggest earnings driver. Segment revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, translating to operating profit of $1.09 billion.

Lenovo has been leveraging demand in the U.S., where the largest market opportunity for infrastructure currently resides. That could present challenges for its AI infrastructure business, especially after some cloud-service providers faced severe financial distress and Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections.

Shares of Lenovo have swung wildly in recent quarters, mirroring these concerns. The stock has wiped out the 50% advance it made in the three months ended September, trimming its gains for the year to about 80%.

Despite a memory crunch and rising consumer-electronics prices, Lenovo has handled the headwinds relatively well. Its intelligent-devices group, which includes PCs, smartphones and tablets, posted 15% revenue growth.

That came as global PC shipments fell 20% in July to September, according to industry tracker IDC. Continued supply constraints and the inventory pull-in earlier in the year, as vendors and channels rushed to stock up ahead of memory-chip-driven price hikes, left the quarter with little demand to draw on.

Lenovo remained the world's largest PC maker by shipments during the quarter, with a 23.8% market share.

WHAT HAPPENS IN VEGAS… STAYS ON YOUR SHIRT.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026

New Augmented Reality Clothing Lets Bachelorette Parties Relive Their Las Vegas Adventures Simply by Scanning What They Wore

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What if your bachelorette party didn't have to end when you left Las Vegas? What if the pictures, videos, and unforgettable moments from your weekend could come back to life simply by scanning your shirt?

That's the idea behind Receipts™, a new augmented reality (AR) clothing collection introduced by Las Vegas–based Naked City Couture and the AR Trading Card Company.

The concept turns ordinary clothing into something extraordinary: a wearable collection of personal memories.

Here's how it works.

A bride and her friends select their favorite designs from the Receipts™ collection. They head to Las Vegas, celebrate, and capture their adventures in photographs and videos.

Everyone uploads their favorite moments to a shared link.

Then comes the crazy.

Scan the clothing with a smartphone, and the party comes back to life in augmented reality.

The pictures. The videos. The laughter. The moments nobody wants to forget.

The same clothing that went to Las Vegas becomes a lasting souvenir, capable of bringing the entire experience back to life.

"People spend thousands of dollars creating memories in Las Vegas, and most of those memories end up buried in their phones,", says Jamie Klingler, Art Director at AR Trading Card Company. "We decided to put them somewhere a little more interesting. On the clothes they wore while making them."

Unlike traditional souvenir shirts, Receipts™ combines fashion with personal multi-media digital content, giving friends a new way to share and revisit their experiences long after the trip ends.

Although designed for vacations, celebrations, and group adventures, the concept is particularly suited to Las Vegas bachelorette parties, where matching outfits and memorable experiences are practically a tradition.

The shirt isn't just something you wore to the party. It's how you bring the party back.

Naked City Couture is available online.

Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, the AR Trading Card Company develops interactive consumer products combining physical merchandise with augmented reality technology. Its Naked City Couture collection transforms everyday apparel into personalized, interactive keepsakes.

data.title: Lenovo Group: Q2 Financial Results 2026/27
data.description:
Lenovo Group: Q2 Financial Results 2026/27

Lenovo delivers record Q2 performance, confident in long-term Hybrid AI opportunities

Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries (‘the Group’), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group’s business fundamentals.

Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income[1] was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue[2] grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.

Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group’s diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group’s profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.

The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.

Market Outlook

Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.

Lenovo’s Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.

Chairman and CEO quote – Yuanqing Yang:

“Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year.”

CFO quote – Winston Cheng:

“Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo’s geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.”

Q2 results:

Intelligent Devices Group (IDG):

  • Revenue for IDG increased 15% year-on-year to record second fiscal quarter revenue of US$17.4 billion, with double-digit year-on-year revenue growth from PCs and smart devices.
  • IDG’s industry-leading operating margin was well maintained at 7.1%, despite a challenging market environment, reflecting the Group’s operational excellence, supply chain resilience, and continued innovation.
  • Global PC market share leadership was further strengthened, reaching 23.8% and extending Lenovo’s lead over the #2 player to an all-time high of more than seven percentage points.
  • The smartphone business delivered record second-quarter revenue, with double-digit year-on-year growth.

Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG):

  • ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded to a record 9.6%.
  • ISG strengthened its global market leadership in traditional server, ranking number one in global x86 server shipments for the first time with 16%[3] market share, up six percentage points year-on-year.
  • Enterprise & SMB revenue grew 200% year-on-year. GPU server revenue grew more than 300% year-on-year, supported by a pipeline that grew 48% quarter-on-quarter to US$80 billion.
  • In the first full quarter as part of the Lenovo Group, Infinidat delivered its best quarter ever – with the high-end storage portfolio expanding ISG’s enterprise storage capabilities.

Solutions and Services Group (SSG):

  • SSG delivered record quarterly revenue of US$3.1 billion, up 20% year-on-year, and surpassing US$3 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded 3.7 percentage points to a record 26%.
  • SSG is growing nearly 2x faster than the broader services market, an outperformance increasingly being driven by higher-value segments as enterprise AI-led offerings accelerate. Managed Services, Projects & Solutions reached a record 63% of SSG revenue, demonstrating the strength of SSG’s tech-led, labor-light model.
  • AI Services continued to deliver triple-digit year-on-year revenue growth, as SSG scaled repeatable AI-powered solutions and Lenovo IP across industries, with momentum in areas including retail, manufacturing and sports.
  • AI Library is also scaling proven, validated use cases across industries and functions, helping customers move from AI experimentation to measurable business outcomes up to 24 times faster.

Corporate highlights

Achievements, announcements, and notable commitments over the past quarter include:

  • Lenovo climbed 43 places to #153 on Fortune’s annual Global 500 List, making it the highest ranking in the company’s history and one of the most significant advances in recent years. The recognition underscores Lenovo’s position as one of the world’s 500 largest companies by revenue.
  • Lenovo received the highest possible rating by Hang Seng Indexes company advancing from its AA+ rating of last year to AAA this year, as well as the highest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores for any company within the technology industry.
  • The Group was named to TIME’s World’s Best Companies 2026 list for the first time, ranking no. 51 globally among leading companies worldwide. The ranking, developed by TIME in partnership with Statista, recognizes top-performing companies around the world based on three primary dimensions: employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. Lenovo achieved an overall score of 87.51, with its growth performance categorized as “Very High.”
  • For the third year in a row, Fast Company recognized Lenovo among its annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The Group was named as a finalist in both the Best Workplaces for Innovators: AI, Automation and Machine Learning Excellence and Best Workplaces for Innovators: North America categories.
  • Lenovo has been recognized as a World’s Top Disability Inclusive business through the Disability Index, the world’s leading benchmarking tool for measuring and advancing disability inclusion in business.
  • Tech World, Lenovo’s annual global innovation event, will return to CES® 2027 in Las Vegas. Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.

About Lenovo

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Guided by its vision of “Smarter Technology for All”, Lenovo is executing a Hybrid AI strategy that spans Personal AI – one personal AI, multiple devices; and Enterprise AI – helping customers turn data into insights and value. This strategy is delivered through the Group’s commitment to world-class innovation and a full-stack AI portfolio, including devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets, accessories), infrastructure solutions (server, storage, edge, high-performance computing and software defined infrastructure), as well as software, solutions, and services. With a global footprint spanning more than 20 research and development locations and a global supply chain that includes more than 30 manufacturing sites across 11 markets, Lenovo is widely recognized for its operational excellence. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY). Learn more at www.lenovo.com and follow the latest news in our newsroom.
